newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-ZAMALEK AND PIRATES HEAD AFRICAN DRAW LIST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAMALEK AND PIRATES HEAD AFRICAN DRAW LIST.

text.p: Egypt's Zamalek and Orlando Pirates of South Africa, the last two winners of Africa's top club prize, will be the seeded teams for Tuesday's draw of the first African Champions' League, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) said on Monday.
Zamalek, the only team to have won the African Champions' Cup four times, are the trophy holders while the Pirates, who hail from Soweto, were dramatic winners in 1995.

They will each head a group of four clubs in the new format for the 33-year-old cup competition, which is taking its cue from the successful and financially lucrative conversion of the European Cup into the European Champions' League.
Zamalek and Pirates, who won the trophy in their first year of African competition, lead eight African clubs who have qualified through two knockout rounds to play in the Champions' League.

The line-up includes three other former cup winners, Raja Casablanca of Morocco, Algeria's Mouloudia Alger and Club Africain of Tunisia as well as Goldfields of Ghana, who have won two successive championships in their domestic league.
Outsiders Ferroviario Maputo from Mozambique and the Angolan team Primiero Agosto complete the list.
Ferroviario, a club owned by the state railway, edged out Cameroon's Unisport Bafang in the second round last month to qualify for the league.
But their shock result was overshadowed by the drubbing meted out by the Angolans to highly-fancied Africa Sports from the Ivory Coast, among the pre-tournament favourites.
Primiero Agosto beat Africa Sports 6-1 on aggregate over two legs in last month's second round, with a hat-trick from striker Mwanza in the second leg at home.
The eight sides, who will earn a minimum of $125,000 for reaching this stage of the competition, will be drawn into two groups in Cairo on Tuesday.
The groups will be decided on a league format, starting in August and concluding on the first weekend of November.
The group winners will go through to the final, to be played over two legs in December.
Under a $3-million sponsorship and television deal the eight clubs will also share a pot of $450,000 for points earned in the Champions' League and the two finalists will earn an extra $225,000 each.
It is the first time that prize money is being offered in the history of the tournament.
The draws for the quarter-finals of Africa's two other club competitions, the Cup Winners' Cup and the CAF Cup, will also be made in Cairo on Tuesday.
These will continue to be played on a two-legged knockout basis.
